 How to do it

using a stripped 30 pin apple cable, inside you will find 4 wires:red,black,white and green.Solder the red wire to a vsys pin(pin 39\) and the black wire to a gnd(ground) pin(for example pin 38\) this way the pico can receive power meanwhile a keyboard can be plugged in.isolate the green and white wires with:[https://www.bol.com/nl/nl/p/krimpkous-assortiment-560-delig-45mm-meerkleurig/9300000021922274/](https://www.bol.com/nl/nl/p/krimpkous-assortiment-560-delig-45mm-meerkleurig/9300000021922274/) (also do this with al the other connections)

Step 1: Solder the VGA Color Network Look at the back of the VGA connector (the side with the hollow solder cups) and locate the small pin numbers. \- Red (VGA Pin 1): Solder a 1k Ohm resistor to GP0 (Pin 1). Solder a 470 Ohm resistor to GP1 (Pin 2). Connect the other ends of both resistors together, cover with heat shrink, and solder them into VGA Pin 1\. \- Green (VGA Pin 2): Solder a 1k Ohm resistor to GP2 (Pin 4). Solder a 470 Ohm resistor to GP3 (Pin 5). Connect the other ends together, cover with heat shrink, and solder them into VGA Pin 2\. \- Blue (VGA Pin 3): Solder a 1k Ohm resistor to GP4 (Pin 6). Solder a 470 Ohm resistor to GP5 (Pin 7). Connect the other ends together, cover with heat shrink, and solder them into VGA Pin 3\. Step 2: VGA Sync and Ground Use regular solid core wire here (no resistors). \- H-Sync: Solder a wire directly from GP6 (Pin 9\) to VGA Pin 13\. \- V-Sync: Solder a wire directly from GP7 (Pin 10\) to VGA Pin 14\. \- Ground (GND): Connect VGA pins 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10 together with a piece of wire. Solder one main wire from this point to a GND pin on the Pico (e.g., Pin 38). Step 3: Build the Audio Filter Cut the AUX cable and strip the wires. Pay close attention to the capacitor polarity: the long leg is positive (+), the short leg with the stripe is negative (-). \- Left (White or Green AUX wire): Solder a 270 Ohm resistor to GP20 (Pin 26). Connect the other end of the resistor to the long leg (+) of the capacitor. Solder the short leg (-) of the capacitor to the White/Green AUX wire. \- Right (Red AUX wire): Solder a 270 Ohm resistor to GP21 (Pin 27). Connect the other end of the resistor to the long leg (+) of the second capacitor. Solder the short leg (-) of the capacitor to the Red AUX wire. \- Audio Ground: Solder the bare copper ground wire of the AUX cable to a GND pin on the Pico (e.g., Pin 28). Step 4: External Power Supply Strip your old Apple 30-pin cable (or any old USB cable). \- Solder the Red wire (+5V) to the VSYS pin (Pin 39). \- Solder the Black wire (GND) to a free GND pin (Pin 40). \- Isolate the remaining green and white wires using heat shrink tubing. Step 5: Shrink and Double-Check Slide heat shrink tubing over all exposed resistor legs and solder joints (especially behind the VGA plug so the pins don't touch). Use a lighter or heat gun to shrink them tightly.   
                        
                        Flashing  
Flashing:

1. Unplug the 30-pin cable from the USB phone charger.  
2. Hold down the BOOTSEL button on the Pico.  
3. While holding the button, plug the USB a end of the apple cable directly into your computer.  
4. Release the BOOTSEL button. The Pico will now mount as a USB drive on your computer.  
5. Download and flash the files from:

[https://github.com/xrip/pico-doom/releases](https://github.com/xrip/pico-doom/releases)

and ur set\! btw heat up all the copper wires to melt off the protective layer

 Game Controls Once everything is connected, use these keyboard controls to play: \- \*\*Move / Turn:\*\* Arrow Keys (Up, Down, Left, Right) \- \*\*Shoot:\*\* Ctrl Key \- \*\*Open Doors / Use Switches:\*\* Spacebar \- \*\*Switch Weapons:\*\* Number Keys 1 to 7 \- \*\*Strafe (Step Sideways):\*\* Hold Alt while pressing Left/Right Arrow Keys
